title: Read a Clay table's column graph before editing it or showing it
hypothesis: The table's columns chained end to end.
change: Parsed every column's inputs into run order with tools/table_graph.py.
result: On the Sabo table people search fed nothing (a hand bridge), two email chains ran in parallel, five columns were dead, and there was no Status or condensed contact column.
next_decision: Bind people search to a buyer-picking formula, then Findymail, then ZeroBounce, and add Status and one contact column before a client sees it.
check: Run python3 -I tools/table_graph.py on the table id before editing a table or showing it, and fix what its lint prints.
scope: Any Clay table a person or client will read.
